Distribution: As far as we know, this subspecies is restricted to the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta (Colombia), but its occurrence in the Sierra de Perijá cannot be discarded a priori. Wojtusiak & Rey (1999) point out that “ most cloud forest and Páramo species found in the Tamá have their relatives in the eastern Cordillera [of Colombia], particularly the Cocuy area, and in the Perijá range ”. Males of Catasticta rochereaui can be differentiated from males of C. cinerea by the white discal bands on both DFW and DHW. Females of C. rochereaui, apart from being much larger, can be easily differentiated from females of C. cinerea by the large yellow anal area on DHW, while in C. cinerea the same area is dark brown with, at most, a few yellow scales.
